I have been around longer than most folks here. I will get right to my point - once upon a time there was a website not unlike Voat called answerology. It was pretty amazing and it was around before Facebook was a big thing. It was small, people were like-minded (mostly), people were tribal, and they made friendships and had debates - just like Voat. Ultimately, it was a combination of a few things that undid that site. You can look into the demise of answerology yourself, but I will focus on the community angle and the business model.

Over time, the community became fixated on a very few users/mods. The mods there were mostly anonymous as there were no "subs" as we know them here. So factions developed. And "flame wars" happened. And people started leaving. As one might imagine, a bunch of SJW's infiltrated and ruined the place. The admins had to bear the ultimate responsibility as they control what mods can and cannot do.

Moderation is a key thing for a site like this. And too many times the moderation and administration of mods has been allowed to go too far beyond community expectations here on Voat. Some of the stuff with abusive mods was handled very well, but only after it went too far. Not a criticism, more of an observation.

There is so much more to say about admin/mod responsibilities, but ultimately answerology was bought by Hearst and they just stopped investing in the site. The brand was quite good, they had a decent community, and it was well established and growing at one point. But because Hearst is an old school media company that probably thought it would be "hip" or "cool" to invest in such a property so they could get into the "online space" thye just did not get it. I guarantee most of their management just stood around thinking about ways to monetize it,rather than to nurture the community and grow it. So it was just left there to bleed out for reasons no one has been able to explain, my feeble attempt here notwithstanding. They could have monetized it with ad revenue, but they did not. They could have hired a relatively inexpensive admin team and a leader with the savvy to run things, but they did not. Voat has that going for it - for now.

Having been a part of several startups, I have seen this challenge many times. There is no angel investor for a site like this. There could be, but that is wishful thinking. One does not simply find an angel by posting about it. This takes networking with the right people, it takes leadership, it takes marketing, and it takes a plan. The folks here cannot tell the difference between a 12 year old kid and a seasoned professional among its user base. I am not saying I can always tell this myself! But one can tell a lot more about a person's gravitas by their posts than one might think. Angel investors are not lurking around Voat. They just aren't. Even those who might have the money, would likely already have reached out.

Minds.com is raising funds right now in an interesting way. But that is a daunting and expensive process. Crowdfunding is good, but limited. What happens when that cash runs out? Voat needs a business plan - and that starts with a business model. I do not see one here and any angel will ask the same question.

My posts seem to fall flat around here most of the time, so I do not expect anyone to take note. But this is my small contribution to the cause: Write a plan and be strategic. This is an exciting time to be around and with FB and Eddit being so vulnerable, you might not get another shot at this. Others are noting the same opportunity - Minds, Gab.ai and others are making huge pushes to fill the void that is being left by FB and others as they become increasingly oppressive.

So, why I am okay with Voat failing - every single time something like this has failed, I have found a much better alternative. The demise of Answerology was what pushed me to Reddit. The demise of Reddit is what brought me here. The limits of interaction here are what pushed me to Minds and others. My eyeballs have value and my posts have value. I will go to the place that demonstrates the most appreciation for my input.

Every other single user is here for some version of the very same thing - Engagement.

Good luck.
